sentences.en: I'll take a coffee.

sentences.en: The thing that distinguishes this place compared to all the rest in Minneapolis that are a lot like it is that when I visited in the spring, there were no prices on the menu.
sentences.zh: 这家店与明尼阿波利斯其他许多类似餐厅的区别在于，我春天去的时候，菜单上没有标价。

sentences.en: And so how do you know what to pay?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么知道该付多少钱呢？

sentences.zh: 你怎么知道东西值多少钱？

sentences.en: Well, like at any restaurant, you receive at the end of the meal something that looks like a check.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像在任何餐厅一样，你在用餐结束时会收到一张看起来像账单的东西。

sentences.en: And what it is is really a solicitation to pay what you can, pay what you decide that you can afford.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一种请求，让你付你所能付的，付你认为自己负担得起的金额。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And on the day that I visited, I'd say half the people that were in the restaurant, according to its owner, couldn't afford to pay and didn't.
sentences.zh: 据店主说，我那天去的时候，餐厅里有一半的人付不起钱，也就没付。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This is deeply un-restaurant-like.
sentences.zh: 这太不像一家餐厅了。

sentences.en: It is un-restaurant-like.
sentences.zh: 确实不像餐厅。

sentences.en: It would seem antithetical to making money.
sentences.zh: 这似乎与赚钱背道而驰。

sentences.en: And in some ways, the move was made as a reaction to how hard it is to make money in restaurants.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这一举措是对餐饮业赚钱之难的一种反应。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》周日版。

sentences.en: There are a couple of key things to understand about the American restaurant industry right now.
sentences.zh: 目前关于美国餐饮业有几个关键点需要了解。

sentences.en: And they can seem contradictory.
sentences.zh: 而且它们看起来似乎是矛盾的。

sentences.en: Menu prices are higher than ever.
sentences.zh: 菜单价格比以往任何时候都高。

sentences.en: Yet restaurant owners are barely scraping by.
sentences.zh: 然而餐厅老板们却几乎入不敷出。

sentences.en: And that's because the business of dining out is in crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是因为餐饮业正处于危机之中。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Brett Anderson, one of the journalists behind The Times' annual Best Restaurant List, explains where this crisis comes from
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事布雷特·安德森，也就是《时报》年度最佳餐厅榜单背后的记者之一，将解释这场危机的根源，

sentences.en: and all the creative ways that restauranteurs are trying to fix it.
sentences.zh: 以及餐馆老板们正在尝试的各种创造性的解决方法。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, October 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月4日，星期日。

sentences.en: Brett Anderson, welcome to The Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 布雷特·安德森，欢迎来到《周日每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: So, you spend a lot of time in restaurants.
sentences.zh: 所以，你花了很多时间在餐厅里。

sentences.en: You're a member of this SEAL Team 6 that drops into entire regions of the United States.
sentences.zh: 你是这支深入美国各个地区的“海豹突击队”成员。

sentences.en: And you quietly, stealthily scout for the best restaurants and then you publish them as this coveted liSt.
sentences.zh: 你悄悄地、隐秘地搜寻最好的餐厅，然后把它们作为这份令人垂涎的榜单发布出来。

sentences.en: Coveted if you're on it.
sentences.zh: 如果你榜上有名，那确实令人垂涎。

sentences.en: Painful if you're not.
sentences.zh: 如果没上榜，那就很痛苦了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This year, I traveled to 19 states for more locations.
sentences.zh: 今年，我为了寻找更多地点去了19个州。

sentences.en: I honestly lost count.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我都数不清了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You know, looking for restaurants to write about for The Times and also just like looking for stories, too, to write for The Times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，既是为了寻找要为《时报》撰写的餐厅，也是为了寻找要为《时报》报道的故事。

sentences.en: Because beyond drawing up lists, you cover the entire industry, which is what we really want to talk with you about here.
sentences.zh: 因为除了制定榜单，你还报道整个行业，这正是我们今天想和你谈论的重点。

sentences.en: So, how did you end up hearing about this restaurant in Minneapolis that's breaking so many basic rules of the economics of the industry?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是怎么听说明尼阿波利斯这家打破了这么多行业经济基本规则的餐厅的？

sentences.en: Well, I'd known about the restaurant for years for the simple reason that I'm from the Twin Cities.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我多年前就知道这家餐厅了，原因很简单，我来自双子城。

sentences.en: I get there to visit family as well as for work.
sentences.zh: 我去那里既是为了探亲，也是为了工作。

sentences.en: And I was in the Twin Cities doing some reporting on the ICE operation in the area that a lot of the listeners will recall made a lot of news.
sentences.zh: 当时我在双子城报道该地区的移民及海关执法局（ICE）行动，很多听众可能还记得，那件事当时引起了很大轰动。

sentences.en: People in the area felt it was akin to something like an occupation.
sentences.zh: 当地人觉得这就像是一种占领。

sentences.en: And Dylan Alverson, who owns Modern Times, had decided in the aftermath of the killing of Alex Preddy, which is when I was there, that he was going to remove prices from his menu.
sentences.zh: 而“现代时代”的老板迪伦·阿尔弗森，在亚历克斯·普雷迪被杀后的余波中——也就是我当时在那里的时候——决定从菜单上取消价格。

sentences.en: He said it was a protest against what he called a fascist economy.
sentences.zh: 他说这是对所谓“法西斯经济”的抗议。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I wanted to stop while we had federally armed troops acting aggressively towards our citizens.
sentences.zh: 当联邦武装部队对我们的公民采取侵略性行动时，我想停止（这种行为）。

sentences.en: I wanted to stop contributing to it financially.
sentences.zh: 我想停止在经济上支持它。

sentences.en: He was doing something that a lot of people in the Twin Cities were doing at that time, which was using what he had to try to do what he could.
sentences.zh: 他当时做的事情和双子城的许多人一样，就是利用他所拥有的资源，尽他所能去做些什么。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: We started this out of a protest, and we're seeing that it evolves into these different ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们最初是出于抗议才开始这样做的，现在我们看到它演变成了这些不同的想法。

sentences.en: And in that conversation, he told me that he had been struggling to make a profit at his restaurant for many years now.
sentences.zh: 在谈话中，他告诉我，多年来他一直难以让餐厅盈利。

sentences.en: I have been poring over these numbers since the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 自疫情以来，我一直在仔细研究这些数字。

sentences.en: And that even though he was busy all the time, even though he was generating what seemed to be quite a bit of revenue, he was simply not able to pay his bills
sentences.zh: 尽管他一直很忙，尽管他创造了看起来相当可观的收入，但他根本无法支付账单，

sentences.en: and simply not able to pay himself very much.
sentences.zh: 也根本无法给自己发多少工资。

sentences.en: And I don't believe that in America
sentences.zh: 我不认为在美国，

sentences.en: restaurants are capable of achieving a profit anymore.
sentences.zh: 餐厅还有能力实现盈利。

sentences.en: What he was explaining to me is something I've heard from restauranteurs across the country in recent years again and again and again,
sentences.zh: 他向我解释的情况，是我近年来从全国各地的餐馆老板那里一次又一次听到的，

sentences.en: which is that the business model isn't working.
sentences.zh: 那就是商业模式行不通了。

sentences.en: We're struggling to stay alive.
sentences.zh: 我们正在挣扎着生存。

sentences.en: And in fact, we don't know if we can.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们不知道自己是否能撑下去。

sentences.en: And so this is like a reset.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一次重置。

sentences.en: This is saying like, how do we stop monetizing our staff?
sentences.zh: 这就像是在说，我们如何停止将员工货币化？

sentences.en: And how do we stop monetizing our customers and have interactions that are based on, I mean, it's true hospitality.
sentences.zh: 我们如何停止将顾客货币化，并进行基于——我是说，真正的热情好客的互动？

sentences.en: And what had looked on paper to be a pretty radical thing, as he explained it to me, it sounded less radical.
sentences.zh: 正如他向我解释的那样，纸面上看起来非常激进的事情，听起来就不那么激进了。

sentences.en: Hmm, so he was kind of throwing up his hands and saying, as a restaurant that can't make this math work anymore,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以他有点束手无策，说作为一家无法再让账目平衡的餐厅，

sentences.en: I'm going to try something new.
sentences.zh: 我要尝试一些新的东西。

sentences.en: I'm just going to take prices off the menu.
sentences.zh: 我打算把菜单上的价格去掉。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's why I wanted to open a restaurant in this neighborhood, was to provide a community space that people could use that lived in this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我想在这个社区开一家餐厅，是为了提供一个住在这个社区的人们可以使用的公共空间。

sentences.en: And the economy has been making it near impossible to continue doing that.
sentences.zh: 而经济状况使得继续这样做变得几乎不可能。

sentences.en: And what was further interesting there is that in doing that by not charging, his business started to do better than it ever had, or better than it has in recent years.
sentences.zh: 更有趣的是，通过不收费，他的生意开始比以往任何时候，或者说比近年来都要好。

sentences.en: Huh, he was doing better financially by letting people pay what they want by not charging.
sentences.zh: 哈，他通过让人们随心所欲地付费，通过不收费，反而获得了更好的经济效益。

sentences.en: By not charging, he had told me 50% of his clientele was not paying for food.
sentences.zh: 通过不收费，他告诉我他50%的顾客没有付餐费。

sentences.en: And he was still doing better than before.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然比以前做得更好。

sentences.en: He had attracted so many donations
sentences.zh: 他吸引了如此多的捐款，

sentences.en: that he was effectively more profitable than he had been when he was charging for food.
sentences.zh: 以至于他实际上比收费时更赚钱了。

sentences.en: That is truly counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这确实非常反直觉。

sentences.en: It struck me as a very illustrative commentary
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得是一个非常生动的评论，

sentences.en: on how little money restaurants are actually making in this economy in the United States.
sentences.zh: 关于在美国当前的经济环境下，餐厅实际上赚的钱是多么少。

sentences.en: I've covered restaurants for over 30 years now.
sentences.zh: 我报道餐厅已经超过30年了。

sentences.en: And I've talked to a lot of restauranteurs.
sentences.zh: 我和很多餐馆老板谈过。

sentences.en: You hear a lot of complaints when you're a reporter, as you know.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，作为一名记者，你会听到很多抱怨。

sentences.en: But it has never been as pervasive.
sentences.zh: 但从来没有像现在这样普遍。

sentences.en: The economic reality has become the dominant narrative in an industry and a culture that I've covered where for decades, the dominant narrative
sentences.zh: 经济现实已经成为我所报道的行业和文化中的主导叙事，而在几十年来，主导叙事

sentences.en: was creative expression, was hospitality, was sense of place.
sentences.zh: 是创意表达、热情好客和地方感。

sentences.en: Now, I believe that that has flipped.
sentences.zh: 现在，我相信情况已经反转了。

sentences.en: And while it might not be apparent to diners so much, it is very much to me in the perspective I have as a reporter.
sentences.zh: 虽然这对食客来说可能不太明显，但从我作为记者的角度来看，情况确实如此。

sentences.en: These restaurants are struggling to survive.
sentences.zh: 这些餐厅正在挣扎求生。

sentences.en: And in fact, many of the people I talk to fear that they might not be able to.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我交谈过的许多人都担心他们可能无法生存下去。

sentences.en: Well, Brett, we want to talk about
sentences.zh: 好吧，布雷特，我们想谈谈

sentences.en: what happened to bring restaurants in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是什么导致美国的餐厅

sentences.en: to this pretty dire place.
sentences.zh: 陷入了如此糟糕的境地。

sentences.en: And now, very much in search of a new business model.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们非常渴望一种新的商业模式。

sentences.zh: 我们将在休息后讨论这个问题。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Restaurants have always been a pretty low-margin business.
sentences.zh: 餐厅一直是一个利润率很低的行业。

sentences.en: So let's talk about how the last few years really exposed not just how low-margin they are, but basically how broken the restaurant industry
sentences.zh: 所以让我们谈谈过去几年是如何真正暴露了它们不仅利润率低，而且基本上餐饮业已经变得多么破碎，

sentences.en: has become and led to all these efforts to reinvent it.
sentences.zh: 并导致了所有这些重塑它的努力。

sentences.en: Well, this chicken little narrative, as someone in the industry described it to me recently, really dates to the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如业内人士最近向我描述的那样，这种“天塌下来”的叙事确实可以追溯到新冠疫情。

sentences.en: But its roots go back decades further and really to the beginning of what many would call the American restaurant revolution.
sentences.zh: 但它的根源可以追溯到几十年前，真正追溯到许多人所说的美国餐厅革命的开始。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Tell us that story.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲那个故事吧。

sentences.en: Well, you've got to think back to the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得回想一下20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: I'll use an example that maybe a lot of people will recognize.
sentences.zh: 我举个例子，可能很多人都会有共鸣。

sentences.en: Chez Panisse restaurant in Berkeley, California.
sentences.zh: 加州伯克利的 Chez Panisse 餐厅。

sentences.en: It still exists.
sentences.zh: 它至今仍在营业。

sentences.en: It's a famous restaurant.
sentences.zh: 那是一家名店。

sentences.en: It's a historically important restaurant that really helped launch what we consider the sort of the farm-to-table movement in the United States.
sentences.zh: 它在历史上意义重大，真正推动了我们现在所说的美国“从农场到餐桌”运动的兴起。

sentences.en: Alice Waters, its chef and owner, got that restaurant off the ground with a $10,000 loan from her father.
sentences.zh: 它的主厨兼老板爱丽丝·沃特斯（Alice Waters）当年靠着她父亲提供的 1 万美元贷款创办了这家餐厅。

sentences.en: She opened that restaurant with flea market items, second-hand furniture.
sentences.zh: 她是用跳蚤市场淘来的旧货和二手家具开起这家店的。

sentences.en: This was a bohemian impulse.
sentences.zh: 这是一种波西米亚式的冲动。

sentences.en: And oddly affordable.
sentences.zh: 而且出奇地负担得起。

sentences.en: It was oddly affordable at a time when urban living was affordable.
sentences.zh: 在那个城市生活成本还很低廉的年代，它确实出奇地亲民。

sentences.en: I'm old enough to remember one of the reasons I wanted to move to a city in my 20s from the suburbs is was it was cheaper
sentences.zh: 我年纪够大，还记得我二十多岁时想从郊区搬到城里的原因之一，就是城里更便宜，

sentences.en: on top of the fact that it was just more interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 更不用说它对我而言本身就更有趣。

sentences.en: And restaurants as we know them really arise from this model.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所熟知的餐厅模式，其实就是从那时兴起的。

sentences.en: You saw restaurants everywhere in all communities, particularly in urban areas, where the business was hinged to the personality of the chef,
sentences.zh: 你随处可见各种社区餐厅，尤其是在城市地区，它们的生意与主厨的个人魅力紧密相连，

sentences.en: the sort of talent and even the ethics of the chef.
sentences.zh: 也与主厨的才华甚至职业操守息息相关。

sentences.en: That became part of the identity of the place.
sentences.zh: 这成了餐厅身份认同的一部分。

sentences.en: And that business model was built on a really different economy, particularly a really different urban economy.
sentences.zh: 而那种商业模式建立在一种截然不同的经济环境之上，尤其是截然不同的城市经济环境。

sentences.en: Meaning what exactly?
sentences.zh: 具体是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, let me give another example.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我再举个例子。

sentences.en: Lutece, this is a New York restaurant.
sentences.zh: Lutece，这是纽约的一家餐厅。

sentences.en: The former restaurant critic of the New York Times,
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的前任餐厅评论家，

sentences.en: Mimi Sheridan, once called the best French restaurant in America,
sentences.zh: 咪咪·谢里丹（Mimi Sheridan）曾称其为美国最好的法餐厅。

sentences.en: Andre Soltner, the famous chef who ran the place, purchased it from its original owner in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 经营这家店的著名主厨安德烈·索尔特纳（Andre Soltner）在 20 世纪 70 年代从原主人手中买下了它。

sentences.en: Not with a bank loan, but with money he saved from working as a chef.
sentences.zh: 不是靠银行贷款，而是靠他当主厨攒下的钱。

sentences.en: And with that money, he was able to purchase not just a restaurant, but a four-story townhouse in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 有了那笔钱，他不仅买下了一家餐厅，还买下了曼哈顿的一栋四层联排别墅。

sentences.en: Now, imagine someone today in New York making only working wages, being able to squirrel away enough money to do something like that.
sentences.zh: 现在，试想一下，今天在纽约，有谁只靠打工薪水就能攒下足够的钱去做这种事？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So what you're really saying is that at the birth of the modern restaurant scene was an affordable urban real estate market.
sentences.zh: 所以你真正想说的是，现代餐饮业的诞生得益于当时负担得起的城市房地产市场。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And everything that went along with that, not only could you afford to open a restaurant for much less money, but people who worked in restaurants could afford to live nearby
sentences.zh: 随之而来的一切也是如此，不仅开餐厅的成本低得多，而且在餐厅工作的人也负担得起住在附近，

sentences.en: on a restaurant's salary.
sentences.zh: 靠的就是餐厅的工资。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: To give just a recent example about how hard the real estate is,
sentences.zh: 举个最近的例子来说明房地产有多难，

sentences.en: Tom Colicchio, who's a famous chef, many listeners may know him by being, because he's one of the hosts of Top Chef, he closed his flagship New York restaurant,
sentences.zh: 名厨汤姆·科利基奥（Tom Colicchio），很多听众可能因为他是《顶级大厨》（Top Chef）的主持人之一而认识他，他关闭了他的纽约旗舰餐厅，

sentences.en: Kraft, just this summer, citing real estate costs, among other rising costs.
sentences.zh: Kraft，就在今年夏天，理由包括房地产成本在内的各种成本上涨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: This famous chef who has other income streams was not able to afford to run a restaurant in New York City given the cost of running a restaurant in New York City.
sentences.zh: 这位拥有其他收入来源的名厨，在纽约经营餐厅的成本压力下，也无法负担在纽约市继续经营一家餐厅了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And today, real estate is just one in a long list of costs that have gone through the roof for restauranteurs.
sentences.zh: 如今，房地产只是餐饮经营者面临的众多成本中高不可攀的一项。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And the shutdowns during the COVID pandemic really exposed the fragility of this business model and exposed all these costs that restauranteurs feel like they're drowning under.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情期间的停业真正暴露了这种商业模式的脆弱性，也暴露了餐饮经营者感到不堪重负的所有这些成本。

sentences.en: Well, just explain that, because I think we all, on some very superficial level,
sentences.zh: 嗯，解释一下吧，因为我觉得我们所有人，在某种非常肤浅的层面上，

sentences.en: understand that the pandemic was terrible for restaurants because it shut so many of them down for so long.
sentences.zh: 都明白疫情对餐厅来说是毁灭性的，因为它导致那么多餐厅停业了那么久。

sentences.en: But beyond that, what do you mean when you say it exposed the fragility of the whole industry?
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，你说它暴露了整个行业的脆弱性，是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, as we know, these restaurants weren't able to operate in many instances for quite a long time, at least not operate as usual, because people legally weren't allowed to eat
sentences.zh: 嗯，如我们所知，在很多情况下，这些餐厅有很长一段时间无法营业，至少无法正常营业，因为法律规定人们不被允许在

sentences.en: inside restaurants, right?
sentences.zh: 餐厅内用餐，对吧？

sentences.en: You couldn't go them.
sentences.zh: 你没法去那里。

sentences.en: So, you know, you're turning off the spigot on revenues.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你相当于切断了收入来源。

sentences.en: And I took note during the pandemic of how many of the sort of most famous people in the industry, people who you would assume had resources to burn, were talking about
sentences.zh: 疫情期间我注意到，业内许多最知名的人士，那些你认为拥有雄厚资源的人，谈论起这件事时，

sentences.en: as though they could not afford to have their business shut down for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 就好像他们根本无法承受生意停摆六周一样。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that's what I mean about exposing the fragility of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的暴露了它的脆弱性。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: There was no margin.
sentences.zh: 根本没有利润空间。

sentences.en: There was no cushion.
sentences.zh: 没有缓冲余地。

sentences.en: There was no rainy day fund.
sentences.zh: 没有应急储备金。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: What is a restaurant worth if it's not open?
sentences.zh: 如果一家餐厅不营业，它还有什么价值？

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: It turns out not much.
sentences.zh: 结果发现价值寥寥。

sentences.en: So there was also these other things during the pandemic that occurred.
sentences.zh: 所以疫情期间还发生了其他一些事情。

sentences.en: The biggest was the killing of George Floyd and the racial reckoning that followed it.
sentences.zh: 最主要的是乔治·弗洛伊德（George Floyd）被杀事件，以及随之而来的种族清算。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the restaurant industry, we saw some spillover here.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在餐饮业，我们也看到了这种波及效应。

sentences.en: This was an industry that was already roiling from the Me Too movement, which hit restaurants very hard.
sentences.zh: 这个行业当时已经因为“我也是”（Me Too）运动而动荡不安，那场运动对餐厅的打击非常大。

sentences.en: And you had this environment in which restaurateurs were taken to social media to try to pledge their solidarity to the people who were on the streets
sentences.zh: 当时的环境是，餐饮经营者纷纷在社交媒体上表态，试图向街头参与

sentences.en: during the Black Lives Matter movement.
sentences.zh: “黑人的命也是命”（Black Lives Matter）运动的人们表达声援。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That invited employees to jump onto social media as well and point out where some of these restaurant owners perhaps weren't as righteous as they were trying
sentences.zh: 这引得员工们也纷纷涌上社交媒体，指出这些餐厅老板中，有些人或许并不像他们试图

sentences.en: to present themselves to be.
sentences.zh: 表现出的那样正义。

sentences.en: Where they were making complaints about workplace conditions and treatment in the workplace and pay and all the reSt.
sentences.zh: 他们开始抱怨工作环境、职场待遇、薪酬以及其他种种问题。

sentences.en: And it was a very contentious time for restaurateurs and for restaurant employees who had felt that they had been mistreated for so long and saw on the streets
sentences.zh: 那对餐饮经营者和长期感到受虐待的餐厅员工来说，是一个非常充满争议的时期，员工们在全国各地的城市街头

sentences.en: of cities across the country this permission to air their own grievances about their workplaces and how they'd been treated.
sentences.zh: 看到了表达对工作场所不满和自身遭遇的许可。

sentences.en: And this dynamic was one of the factors that caused labor costs to really rise.
sentences.zh: 这种动态是导致劳动力成本大幅上升的因素之一。

sentences.en: You know, people were saying,
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们当时在说，

sentences.en: I'm not going to go back to work at a restaurant.
sentences.zh: “如果我拿不到维持生活的工资，我就不会回餐厅工作。”

sentences.en: If I can't make a living wage.
sentences.zh: “如果我拿不到维持生活的工资。”

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And living wages in a lot of cities is much higher than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 在许多城市，维持生活的工资标准比过去高得多。

sentences.en: And, you know, a recent study that came out last year, industry studies, said that wages are up 41% compared to pre-pandemic levels in the restaurant industry.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，去年发布的一项行业研究显示，餐饮业的工资水平比疫情前上涨了 41%。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Which, of course, is great for workers and perhaps was quite overdue.
sentences.zh: 这对员工来说当然是好事，而且可能早就该涨了。

sentences.en: But from the perspective of a restaurateur who, as you've already established, is dealing with really high real estate costs, is dealing with the hit of the pandemic, is suddenly
sentences.zh: 但从餐饮经营者的角度来看，正如你已经指出的，他们正面临极高的房地产成本，又遭受了疫情的冲击，这突然之间

sentences.en: a very big new expense.
sentences.zh: 成了一笔巨大的新开支。

sentences.en: It's a big new expense.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔巨大的新开支。

sentences.en: And you're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Higher wages we shouldn't see as a net bad.
sentences.zh: 我们不应将工资上涨视为纯粹的坏事。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But it is a challenge for a small business, right?
sentences.zh: 但这对小企业来说确实是个挑战，对吧？

sentences.en: As many restaurants are.
sentences.zh: 毕竟很多餐厅都是小企业。

sentences.en: Even many of the most famous restaurants can be as few as 25 tables.
sentences.zh: 即使是许多最著名的餐厅，可能也只有 25 张桌子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's not the only increased cost that they're facing.
sentences.zh: 而且这还不是他们面临的唯一成本增加。

sentences.en: You may recall during the pandemic, you know, was when we first started seeing, at least in modern times, inflation become a very potent political issue that animated
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得疫情期间，我们开始看到，至少在现代，通货膨胀成为一个非常强烈的政治议题，激发了

sentences.en: a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 很多人的情绪。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We covered it a lot on The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我们在《每日新闻》（The Daily）中对此做了大量报道。

sentences.en: Actually, the government's response to the pandemic, which was instinctive and somewhat natural, which is to pump all this money into the consumer world, ended up making
sentences.zh: 事实上，政府对疫情的反应——本能且在某种程度上是自然的——即向消费领域注入大量资金，最终导致

sentences.en: everything a bit more expensive.
sentences.zh: 一切都变得更贵了。

sentences.en: Yeah, food costs are up
sentences.zh: 是啊，食品成本上涨了

sentences.en: 35% for restaurants compared to pre-pandemic levels.
sentences.zh: 与疫情前相比，餐厅的食品成本上涨了 35%。

sentences.en: And that's a big, big number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常大的数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And particularly for businesses that already had very small margins and whose other costs are also rising.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于那些利润空间本来就很小，且其他成本也在上涨的企业来说。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: There has become,
sentences.zh: 甚至在过去一年半里，

sentences.en: I'd say, in the last year and a half, even, a sort of new form of communication from restaurants on social media where they are taking to their online media feeds
sentences.zh: 餐厅在社交媒体上出现了一种新的沟通方式，他们开始在在线媒体平台上

sentences.en: and trying to communicate with people just how much their costs are rising.
sentences.zh: 试图与人们沟通他们的成本上涨得有多厉害。

sentences.en: There isn't room to sell affordable food in Seattle, and here's why.
sentences.zh: “在西雅图，已经没有空间去卖平价食品了，原因如下。”

sentences.en: I'm thinking specifically last month, there's a restaurant that serves Indian street food in Seattle called Spicewala.
sentences.zh: 我特别想到上个月，西雅图有一家供应印度街头小吃的餐厅叫 Spicewala。

sentences.en: Our cost of goods, which is the cost of anything goes into the food that we serve you, has doubled since 2018.
sentences.zh: “我们的商品成本，也就是我们为你提供的食物所包含的一切成本，自 2018 年以来已经翻了一番。”

sentences.en: And the owner posted to Instagram a video in which he showed all these different ingredients that were up.
sentences.zh: 老板在 Instagram 上发布了一段视频，展示了所有涨价的食材。

sentences.en: The cost of chicken is up 13%.
sentences.zh: 鸡肉成本上涨了 13%。

sentences.en: The percentage increase that they've had to pay.
sentences.zh: 这是他们不得不支付的涨幅百分比。

sentences.en: Potatoes, 54%.
Onions, 89%.
And what he's trying to do there is what a lot of restaurateurs are really struggling to do, which is to communicate with their customers to try to say, look,
sentences.zh: 他试图做的事情，也是许多餐饮经营者正在努力做的，那就是与顾客沟通，试图说明：看，

sentences.en: these rising menu prices are not a result of our greed.
sentences.zh: 这些菜单价格上涨并非因为我们贪婪。

sentences.en: They're really a matter of our own personal survival.
sentences.zh: 这确实关乎我们个人的生存。

sentences.en: We just cannot keep up with these costs.
sentences.zh: 我们实在无法跟上这些成本的上涨。

sentences.en: We cannot operate a profitable business without passing some of that cost on to customers.
sentences.zh: 如果不将部分成本转嫁给顾客，我们就无法维持盈利的业务。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Brett,
sentences.zh: 还有，布雷特（Brett），

sentences.en: I'm surprised you haven't yet brought up credit card fees.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶你还没提到信用卡手续费。

sentences.en: Credit card fees are something you hear a lot of people complain about.
sentences.zh: 信用卡手续费是很多人抱怨的话题。

sentences.en: And it is sort of striking for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说有点令人震惊。

sentences.en: I always just assumed as a consumer that this era in which we've gone to almost a cashless society would be good for retailers.
sentences.zh: 作为消费者，我一直以为我们进入这种几乎无现金的社会时代对零售商来说是好事。

sentences.en: You know, it sort of removes this barrier of like, oh, I don't have enough money in my pocket.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它消除了那种“哦，我口袋里钱不够”的障碍。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And, but that's just not the case for restaurateurs, at least those that I talk to.
sentences.zh: 但对于餐饮经营者来说，至少我交谈过的那些人，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: They increasingly talk about how these 2% to 4% swipe fees are just killing them.
sentences.zh: 他们越来越多地谈到这些 2% 到 4% 的刷卡手续费是如何让他们苦不堪言的。

sentences.en: Times did a story in which it said that that was the third highest cost behind labor and products that restaurants have, are credit card fees.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》曾报道称，信用卡手续费是餐厅继劳动力和产品之后的第三大成本。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And because no one's paying cash ever at all anymore,
sentences.zh: 而且因为现在几乎没人用现金支付了，

sentences.en: every bill involves a credit card fee.
sentences.zh: 每一笔账单都涉及信用卡手续费。

sentences.en: And it's not just credit card fees.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是信用卡手续费。

sentences.en: There are all of these assortment of fees that restaurateurs have to pay to basically all of these industries that have been built on the backs of restaurants.
sentences.zh: 餐饮经营者还必须支付各种各样的费用，基本上是付给所有这些建立在餐厅背后的行业。

sentences.en: Think about delivery apps.
sentences.zh: 想想外卖应用程序。

sentences.en: Think about the food distributors, the reservation platforMs.
sentences.zh: 想想食品分销商、预订平台。

sentences.en: All of these things take a cut.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都要分一杯羹。

sentences.en: I don't think people know that, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我觉得人们并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: But I mean, I use Seamless and it wasn't until I was doing some research for our conversation that I, and I'm embarrassed to say this, I discovered for the very first time that all
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我使用 Seamless，直到我为我们的谈话做研究时，我才发现——说出来真尴尬——我第一次发现所有

sentences.en: these services charge the restaurants basically a commission.
sentences.zh: 这些服务基本上都要向餐厅收取佣金。

sentences.en: Most of the restaurateurs I talk to say that when you order using a delivery app from them, they lose money.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的大多数餐饮经营者都说，当你使用外卖应用程序向他们订餐时，他们是在亏钱。

sentences.en: That they basically consider it a marketing coSt.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上将其视为一种营销成本。

sentences.en: And it's a risky one because if you get your food delivered from a restaurant and it arrives cold or something disappointing happens en route, the customer is going to blame the
sentences.zh: 而且这风险很大，因为如果你从餐厅订外卖，食物送到时凉了，或者途中发生了什么令人失望的事情，顾客更可能会责怪

sentences.en: restaurant more likely than it's going to blame the delivery app.

sentences.zh: 而且与邻居之间也产生了紧张关系。

sentences.en: It was also challenging for the staff.
sentences.zh: 这对员工来说也很有挑战性。

sentences.en: And while I think that the staff, as far as I could tell when I was there, really appreciated that challenge and really wanted to deliver on it, it became quite
sentences.zh: 虽然我认为员工们，据我在那里时的观察，真的很感激这种挑战，也真的很想实现它，但这变得让每个人

sentences.en: physically exhausting for everyone.
sentences.zh: 在体力上都精疲力竭。

sentences.en: Everything
sentences.zh: 一切

sentences.en: culminated to a point where I was like, we just, we have to stop.
sentences.zh: 最终达到一个临界点，我当时想，我们必须停止了。

sentences.en: And so Dylan announced that what he had called postmodern times was going to close down for a break and reopen again in
sentences.zh: 于是 Dylan 宣布他所称的“后现代时期”将关闭休息一段时间，并在

sentences.en: August as modern times with a business model that sort of split the difference between the experiment he was running and the traditional restaurant that that replaced.
sentences.zh: 8月以“现代时期”重新开业，采用一种介于他正在进行的实验和被取代的传统餐厅之间的商业模式。

sentences.en: And split the difference how?
sentences.zh: 那怎么折中呢？

sentences.en: What model did he settle on?
sentences.zh: 他最终确定了什么模式？

sentences.en: Well, there are no prices back on the menu, but he is still, he tells me, giving away 125 free meals a week.
sentences.zh: 虽然菜单上没有恢复标价，但他告诉我，他每周仍会提供125份免费餐食。

sentences.en: He went out and got a grant to help support that particular program, but the prices on the menu are not designed to fuel that charitable effort.
sentences.zh: 他专门申请了一笔拨款来支持这个项目，但菜单上的定价并非为了支撑这项慈善事业。

sentences.en: The prices that are on the menu today, he says, represent the lowest price he can charge and still meet all of his expenses.
sentences.zh: 他说，目前的菜单定价代表了他能收取的最低价格，同时还要能支付所有开销。

sentences.en: So, we reopened with our menu priced at basically a zero profit margin,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们重新开业时，菜单定价基本上是零利润率，

sentences.en: which is a continuation of this idea that I keep pushing that there is no longer a profit margin in restaurants.
sentences.zh: 这延续了我一直强调的一个观点，即餐厅行业已经没有利润空间了。

sentences.en: That we have menu items that are priced cost at
sentences.zh: 我们菜单上的菜品定价成本为

sentences.en: $24 that is reflective of a modest living wage and the real cost of food without a profit involved.
sentences.zh: 24美元，这反映了合理的最低生活工资以及食品的真实成本，不包含任何利润。

sentences.en: So, he is not making money, and therefore, I wonder, is this any kind of pathway forward for the rest of the industry?
sentences.zh: 所以，他并没有赚钱，因此我很好奇，这对整个行业来说算是一种前进的方向吗？

sentences.en: It doesn't sound like it would be.
sentences.zh: 听起来似乎不太像。

sentences.en: Well, he would say otherwise.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他可不这么认为。

sentences.en: He is actually arguing that this new model is something that other restaurants could adopt.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是在论证，这种新模式是其他餐厅可以效仿的。

sentences.en: He is trying to create an example where you have a restaurant that is using donations to feed people who can't afford to feed themselves while still meeting its bills and
sentences.zh: 他试图创造一个范例：餐厅利用捐款为那些无力负担餐费的人提供食物，同时又能支付账单，

sentences.en: paying its employees with the for-profit arm inside that very same restaurant.
sentences.zh: 并利用同一家餐厅内的营利部门来支付员工工资。

sentences.en: If I can create a fundraising mechanism that can raise money to provide hospitality, we can take that program and add restaurants to it.
sentences.zh: 如果我能建立一种筹款机制来提供餐饮服务，我们就可以推广这个项目，并增加更多的餐厅。

sentences.en: He thinks that if other places adopt this model, that it would take some of the burden off his restaurant to be feeding all these people and create some economies of scale.
sentences.zh: 他认为，如果其他地方也采用这种模式，就能减轻他餐厅独自承担供餐的负担，并产生规模经济效应。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, he's saying that the industry's math is so bad that you might as well do something like become a quasi-nonprofit that can pay all your staff, pay all your
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他基本上是在说，这个行业的账算得太差了，你还不如转型成准非营利组织，这样既能支付所有员工工资、支付所有

sentences.en: bills, keep up with the rising food costs and all the fees and commissions, and that might be okay to not have a profit at the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 账单，又能应对不断上涨的食品成本以及各种费用和佣金，而且年底没有利润可能也没关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I have to say, something that he said that really stuck with me is he and his staff, during this challenging time when they were trying to do this radical
sentences.zh: 是的，我必须说，他所说的一件事让我印象深刻，那就是他和他的员工在尝试这种激进做法的这段充满挑战的时期，

sentences.en: thing, discovered that they liked providing this service to people who otherwise weren't able to afford restaurants.
sentences.zh: 发现他们很乐意为那些原本吃不起餐厅的人提供服务。

sentences.en: They appreciated working at a place where that financial barrier had been removed and that was open to everyone in their community regardless of how well-off they were.
sentences.zh: 他们很庆幸能在这样一个消除了经济门槛的地方工作，这里对社区里的每个人开放，无论他们是否富有。

sentences.en: There was something about it that made their work feel more worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉让他们的工作显得更有价值。

sentences.en: We kind of went back to this core idea of hospitality, which is just offering comforts, relationships that are formed
sentences.zh: 我们回到了待客之道的这一核心理念，即提供舒适感，通过邀请人们进来并为他们提供食物，

sentences.en: through inviting people in and feeding them, basically.
sentences.zh: 从而建立起人际关系，基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: And Dylan told me that that's the reason that he's doing this, not because he wants to make a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 迪伦告诉我，这就是他做这件事的原因，而不是因为他想赚很多钱。

sentences.en: Not only does he think that it's not really possible in this economy, but what he's really interested in is providing a space for people to come together and feel human and
sentences.zh: 他不仅认为在当前的经济环境下这几乎不可能，而且他真正感兴趣的是提供一个空间，让人们聚在一起，感受到人性，

sentences.en: feel included and feel safe and satiated for a little portion of their day.
sentences.zh: 感受到被包容，并在一天中的一小段时间里感到安全和满足。

sentences.en: Which is ultimately the very idea at the heart of a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 这归根结底正是餐厅核心的理念。

sentences.en: Indeed, it is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And there are people all over this country that are being
sentences.zh: 而且在这个国家的各个地方，都有人在

sentences.en: really nice to perfect strangers.
sentences.zh: 对完全陌生的人表现出真正的善意。

sentences.en: And, you know, you cover politics a lot on this show.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在节目中经常报道政治。

sentences.en: You know, in that context, in this context of polarization that we live in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在那种背景下，在我们所处的这种两极分化的背景下。

sentences.en: And not nicest to strangers.
sentences.zh: 而且对陌生人并不总是最友好的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I have a deeper appreciation for this business that is founded on
sentences.zh: 我对这个行业有了更深刻的认识，它的基础是

sentences.en: trying to treat people with respect and give them the benefit of the doubt.
sentences.zh: 试图以尊重对待他人，并给予他们信任。

sentences.en: Foundationally, that is their goal.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这就是他们的目标。

sentences.en: That is the goal of restaurants.
sentences.zh: 这就是餐厅的目标。

sentences.en: These experiences of being able to hang out with your friends, being able to escape from whatever it is for a little bit of period of time, for being around people that you
sentences.zh: 这些能够与朋友相聚、能够暂时逃离现实的体验，能够与你不认识的人待在一起，

sentences.en: don't know, being treated well, all of that feels kind of like more essential than it ever has to me before.
sentences.zh: 受到良好的对待，所有这些对我来说比以往任何时候都显得更加重要。

sentences.en: And it makes me think that as challenging as the restaurant business has become,
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得，尽管餐饮业已经变得如此艰难，

sentences.en: I really think that we all should be hoping that we can save it.
sentences.zh: 但我真的认为我们都应该希望能够拯救它。
